as_told.title: Chase Brandon, CIA Hollywood liaison, and his UFO book

plain: The story is that a former CIA man wrote a novel to hint at real secrets about Roswell, the famous 1947 crash in New Mexico, and about a being said to have been found there. The book is The Cryptos Conundrum, and Michels dates it to 2012. Its author is Chase Brandon, a CIA officer who became the agency's liaison to Hollywood, though Michels once calls the name a pseudonym. If true, the CIA's own people let the truth out dressed as fiction. Michels says the book 'talks about Hillenkoetter,' one of the first CIA directors, 'who dealt with Roswell.' He also says it describes a secret committee on NHI (non-human intelligence) and a group inside an Office of Strategic Assessment. Michels says it opens with a Francis Bacon quote: some truths are so strange they have to be hidden in fiction. A researcher named Grant Cameron calls the book 'the Crystal Conundrum.' He says it deals with how the CIA handled the Roswell crash and that, 'according to some of the stories,' the manuscript went through review eight times before it came out.
